title: Maximum Transactions Without Negative Balance
summary: Given an array of transactions with positive values indicating received money and negative values indicating sent money, determine the maximum number of transactions that can be processed without the account balance ever dropping below zero, considering transactions must be processed in order but allowing some to be skipped.
statement: Given an array of transactions with positive values indicating received money and negative values indicating sent money, determine the maximum number of transactions that can be processed without the account balance ever dropping below zero, considering transactions must be processed in order but allowing some to be skipped.
constraints: transactions contains up to 100,000 signed amounts processed in their original order.
Any transaction may be skipped; the running balance starts at zero and may never become negative.
Return the maximum number that can be retained.
hints: When the balance turns negative, at least one selected transaction must be discarded.
Discarding the most negative selected value restores the most balance while losing only one transaction.
Maintain selected values in a min-heap and repeatedly remove its minimum whenever the balance is negative.
The greedy exchange never leaves less balance than removing any other single choice, preserving the best chance to keep all later transactions.
editorial: The greedy exchange never leaves less balance than removing any other single choice, preserving the best chance to keep all later transactions.

tests.explanation: Skipping negative five lets the other four transactions finish with balance two.
Every available transaction would immediately make the balance negative, so keep none.
